archetype: Five-colour Dragon typal battlecruiser with a combat-combo top end routed through Aggravated Assault. deck-audit matches it to the combo template (4-8 tutors, 4-6 protection) on strategic_frame.json's own say-so, and the deck answers with 7 tutors and 6 protection — the frame and the measurement agree.
verdict: This deck has already solved conversion: six checker-passed lines, two of them unbounded combat engines that close from one connecting attacker. What limits it is the fit between a 5-to-7-mana threat base and 4.937 mana on turn six, and the declared fix for that gap — cost reduction — lives on three cards that appear in 19.9% of opening sevens. Underneath that, red carries 46.5% of the pip load on 28.6% of the sources while black is a 7.9% splash paying for two double-black sorceries. Nothing here is broken; the cheapest available wins are two-mana cost reducers and one land swap.

open_questions.question: Can Klauth, Unrivaled Ancient's attack-trigger mana pay for Aggravated Assault's {3}{R}{R} activation? The trigger says 'Spend this mana only to cast spells', and activating an ability is not casting a spell — if it cannot, Klauth is not a third Assault engine and the deck's Assault package is two cards deep, not three.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Both verified Assault loops (003, 006) depend on a specific funding source. Whether Klauth is a third one changes how many cards support the deck's only verified kill, which is the redundancy question the whole diagnosis turns on.

open_questions.question: Hellkite Courser puts The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield from the command zone and returns it there at the next end step. strategic_frame.json claims 'no recast tax accrued' — is that right, and does the commander's own attack trigger fire on the Courser turn?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the deck's only route to a commander that is cast in 13.7% of simulated games by turn ten. If the line works as claimed, Courser is a four-mana capstone and the diagnosis's advice to ignore the nine-mana cast gets stronger, not weaker.

findings.note: I recomputed the tally rather than checking the prose, using manabase.land_colors over the modified 99 (Glacial Fortress removed, Mana Confluence added), expanded by copies. Result: BEFORE W 10 / U 11 / B 11 / R 20 / G 18 at 34 lands — exactly mana_analysis.json; AFTER W 10 / U 11 / B 12 / R 21 / G 19 at 34 lands. land_colors('Mana Confluence') returns all five, Glacial Fortress returns {W, U}, so W goes 10 -> 9 -> 10 and nets ZERO. evidence.land_sources_after.W = 11 is wrong by one. The entry's own prose has it right ('the land counts move W 10->10'), and so does cut_candidates[6].cost_of_cutting ('restores both colours exactly (W 10->10, U 11->11)') — so the machine-readable value is the one field in the document that disagrees with the two prose statements beside it, and it is the same field that carried the iteration-1 error. Everything else in the block is verified correct: B total 16->17, gating colour stays B, axis -20 -> -19 (I recomputed the worst-colour minimum over all five colours against the unchanged source_targets, since no nonland card moved and the pip requirements are therefore identical), and the 34-land count is unchanged.

The prescription itself is now sound and the previous contradicts-artifact finding is closed. Against Forbidden Orchard the swap was source-neutral and the document now says so in its own words ('swapping it for Forbidden Orchard is exactly source-neutral, because mana_analysis.json already counts Forbidden Orchard as producing all five colours'), which is the correction stated rather than quietly patched. Against Glacial Fortress it is not neutral, and closes: 'colour-sources' is now earned: the axis moves. The cross-references hold too — cut_candidates[6] Glacial Fortress is the natural_cut and its cost_of_cutting names Mana Confluence as the refill, cut_candidates[4] Forbidden Orchard now warns that taking both lands the deck at 33, and I confirmed that arithmetic (34 lands, land-for-land swap, minus one more land = 33). 'Pair it with the Panharmonicon cut instead and the deck reaches 35 lands' is also right — Panharmonicon is an artifact, so the Confluence is a net land addition.

The narrowed superlative is true across the WHOLE 99, not just against the three cards it names. I sorted every entry in cards.json by mana value: at 8 or more there are exactly five, one of which is the commander. The other four are Cavern-Hoard Dragon (9, 'Creature — Dragon', and 'This spell costs {X} less to cast, where X is the greatest number of artifacts an opponent controls' — so both a Dragon AND self-reducing), Blasphemous Act (9, Sorcery, 'This spell costs {1} less to cast for each creature on the battlefield' — self-reducing), Utvara Hellkite (8, 'Creature — Dragon'), and Dracogenesis (8, Enchantment, no cost text). So Dracogenesis is the only mana-value-8+ card in the 99 that is neither a Dragon nor self-reducing, and the reducers' oracle text confirms why none reaches it: Urza's Incubator and Herald's Horn reduce creature spells of the chosen type, Dragonspeaker Shaman and eminence reduce Dragon spells. The mana-value-8+ scope is stated explicitly rather than smuggled in as 'expensive', which is what made the old wording false.

I am reversing my iteration-2 over-claimed call on this entry, and recording why rather than quietly dropping it. I had reasoned from the field NAME matching deck_audit's, which computes single_points_of_failure strictly as targets with thinnest_size <= 1 and returns [] here. But the doctor's schema in .claude/agents/deck-doctor.md types the field on 'component', not on a card, and the gishath diagnosis demonstrates the intended semantics: its Forerunner of the Empire entry is a genuine one-card hub sitting inside 7- and 9-card components, which the audit's size test cannot see at all. So the field carries doctor judgment about where the engine fails first, not a mirror of the audit's computation. On that reading this entry qualifies: it is the audit's only thin: true, thinnest: true component, it is labelled with its own count in the body ('Three cards carry the whole curve fix'), and the whole document turns on it. My reversal costs nothing here — this artifact fails on the tally finding regardless — which is why I can make the call on the merits.
